holidays.name: National Pancake Day (Sept. 26 Observance)
holidays.description: A day to flip, stack, and drown flapjacks in syrup, butter, and whatever toppings your breakfast dreams allow. Pancake fans mark the date with stacks at home or at diners.
holidays.origin: Pancakes are among the oldest foods in the world, and various pancake days are claimed on the calendar. This one is an informal, fan-driven observance with no single official founder, and some calendars list it on different dates.
holidays.funFact: Archaeologists found traces of a pancake-like meal in the stomach of Ötzi the Iceman, who lived over 5,000 years ago.

holidays.name: National Johnny Appleseed Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the barefoot, tin-pot-hatted legend who wandered the American frontier planting apple trees. People celebrate with apple pie, cider, and by planting a tree.
holidays.origin: Johnny Appleseed was the nickname of John Chapman, born September 26, 1774, in Leominster, Massachusetts. He became a folk hero for spreading apple orchards across Pennsylvania, Ohio, Indiana, and Illinois.
holidays.funFact: Many of Johnny's apples were not for eating. They were small, tart cider apples, and in frontier days hard cider was the main use.

holidays.name: European Day of Languages
holidays.description: A multilingual celebration across Europe and beyond, encouraging people to learn languages and appreciate linguistic diversity. Expect language games, tasting events, and people saying hello in as many tongues as possible.
holidays.origin: The Council of Europe launched it in 2001, the European Year of Languages, to promote language learning and cultural understanding.
holidays.funFact: Europe is home to roughly 225 indigenous languages, yet the Council of Europe has 24 official languages in the EU alone.

holidays.name: Love Note Day
holidays.description: A sweet and low-tech holiday for sneaking little handwritten notes of affection into lunchboxes, coat pockets, and bathroom mirrors. It rewards tiny gestures with big smiles.
holidays.origin: An informal, unofficial observance popularized through holiday calendars and social media as a way to spread kindness through simple written messages.
holidays.funFact: Handwritten notes are so rare these days that studies suggest recipients often value them more than the sender expects.

holidays.name: Native American Day (California Observance Season)
holidays.description: A day for honoring the heritage, culture, and contributions of Native peoples, often with storytelling, art, dance, and educational events.
holidays.origin: In California it is observed on the fourth Friday of September, which falls close to this date in some years, and it was established to recognize the state's Native American communities.
holidays.funFact: California has one of the largest Native American populations of any U.S. state, with over 100 federally recognized tribes.
